one_month_reasoning: No Salesforce earnings fall in the window (Q2 FY27 was reported 2026-08-26; Q3 FY27 is normally reported in early December). Dreamforce (Sep 15-17) and Investor Day (Sep 16) are already past. Events inside the window: final settlement of the $25B ASR, which the company expects in October 2026 (about 30-37M more shares delivered at an expected average of about $176-182, which is already known and priced in); closing of the Contentful ($1.5B) and Fin/Intercom ($3.6B) deals, which guidance already assumes; and late-October peer software and hyperscaler earnings plus the FOMC, which can move the group. None of these is a strong directional catalyst, so I use a nearly symmetric lognormal centred at about $232 (a slight upward tilt for the small ASR share-count benefit) with monthly sigma of 0.134 (47% annual vol / 3.5).

fair_value.method: Two methods weighted equally, each on estimates about 12 months out: (1) 14.5x P/E on NTM non-GAAP EPS of about $18.3 at Sep-2027, excluding strategic-investment gains, gives $265; (2) a 7.75% equity FCF yield on FY28E FCF/share of about $20.8 gives $268. Blended fair value is about $266.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: NTM (FY29-weighted) non-GAAP EPS ex-investment gains of about $18.3 at Sep-2027 x 14.5x. FY28E EPS $16.7 = revenue $51.0B x 35.0% non-GAAP op margin ($17.85B), less about $1.9B interest, plus $0.3B other income, taxed at 20.5%, over about 775M diluted shares

inputs_detail.derivation: The FY27 midpoint of $46.25B grown about 10%. That is below the 11%+ FY26-30 CAGR implied by the $63B FY30 target (deck slide 26) because Informatica annualizes out of growth. It includes a partial-year contribution from Contentful and Fin and the H2 organic reacceleration management called 'math' on the Q2 call. cRPO +14% in Q2 supports it.
The FY27 guide is 34.3%, and the deck shows about +1,560bps of expansion since FY22 (slide 19). I assume +70bps, held back by dilution from the Contentful and Fin acquisitions and 1,200 new AEs.
Q2 FY27 interest expense was $473M, annualized. The 10-Q debt table shows about $39.3B of notes and term loans after the March 2026 $25B raise at 4.2-5.2% coupons.

Q2 diluted shares were 821M, with 103M initially delivered under the ASR at $198.34 (about 80% of the total). $25B at an expected average of $176-182 means about 137-142M in total, so about 35M more arrive at the October settlement, leaving about 787M. On top of that I assume net open-market buybacks of about 1.5% a year (deck says 'at least 14% expected share count reduction'; $50B authorization).

inputs_detail.input: FY27 non-GAAP EPS excluding investment gains
inputs_detail.derivation: The FY27 guide of $16.67-16.71 less the $2.98 H1 strategic-investment gains disclosed in the release footnote. This is the base for growth checks: FY28E $16.7 is about +22%, mostly from share count.

The stock now trades at about 15x NTM non-GAAP EPS ex-gains (231 / about 15.2; that EPS is my own build from the Q3 guide of $3.43 plus estimated Q4 to Q2). That is far below CRM's historic 20-30x because of the 2026 'SaaSpocalypse' seat-compression discount. I hold the multiple roughly flat because leverage has risen and SBC is still 9% of revenue, and I do not assume a rerating.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: FY28E FCF $16.2B / 780M shares = $20.8 per share, at a 7.75% equity FCF yield

inputs_detail.derivation: Operating income growth of about 12% is offset by a full year of higher cash interest on the $25B of new debt (10-Q). Capex is about 1.5% of revenue per guidance.
The same post-ASR share bridge as the P/E method, taken nearer the start of FY28.

The current yield is about 8.2% (FY27 FCF of $15B / about 790M shares / $231). Management calls the ASR a 40%+ return at a $182 average (slide 25). I allow slight compression, since FCF is after interest but before SBC of about $4.2B.

bear.story: The H2 organic reacceleration fails and cRPO slows to high single digits. Seat compression shows up in Sales and Service Cloud renewals, and Agentforce credit consumption does not offset it. Leverage of about 2x net debt/EBITDA and slower FCF growth pull the multiple to about 10-11x on EPS of about $15.5.

base.story: Revenue grows 10-11% with cRPO at 12-14%, margins edge up to about 35%, and the ASR plus buybacks lift EPS to about $16.7 in FY28 and about $18 NTM. The multiple stays about 14x while the AI-disruption debate stays unresolved.

bull.story: Agentforce and Data 360 ARR grows from about $3.9B to $7B+, NNAOV strength converts into 12%+ organic growth, and the market rerates CRM as an AI winner to about 19x NTM EPS of about $18.5.

thesis_break_reason: Below about $165 (about 10-11x NTM EPS, back toward the 52-week low of $146) the market would be pricing a fall in organic growth and seat erosion that contradicts management's 'Q3 is math' reacceleration commitment and 14% cRPO. Trading there most likely means a real fundamental miss, such as a cRPO guide cut, visible net seat losses or a failed integration of Informatica, Fin or Contentful, and not just ordinary volatility at 47% realized vol.

catalysts.event: Final settlement of the $25B ASR (about 30-37M more shares); Contentful and Fin deals close

key_uncertainties: Whether AI agents compress per-seat revenue faster than Agentforce consumption and premium-edition upgrades add it
How much of the organic reacceleration is real versus acquisitions (Informatica adds about 3-4pts; Contentful and Fin add more)
Much higher leverage after the debt-funded $25B ASR (debt about $39B), and rising interest expense eating into EPS growth
Volatility in strategic-investment gains (a $11.3B portfolio, $2.98/share of H1 EPS) that flatters headline EPS
Leadership turnover in engineering, and further M&A appetite
Sector-wide software multiple sentiment (the 2026 SaaSpocalypse drawdown)
reasoning: Primary documents show a business growing about 11% (about 7-8% organic before Informatica) with cRPO accelerating to 14%, NNAOV at a four-year high, and Agentforce plus Data 360 ARR near $3.9B (+210%). The company guides H2 organic reacceleration and targets $63B+ revenue in FY30. Headline FY27 non-GAAP EPS of $16.69 includes $2.98 of investment gains, so underlying EPS is about $13.7. The financial-engineering lever is large: a debt-funded $25B ASR at about $176-182 retires about 14% of shares, so FY28 EPS rises about 20% even with only about 12% net income growth after about $1.9B of new interest. At $231 the stock trades at about 15x NTM EPS ex-gains and an 8% FCF yield. P/E and FCF-yield methods both point to about $265-268 fair value 12 months out, and the consensus target is $281. I centre the base case slightly below fair value at about $258, because the market has kept the AI seat-compression discount all year and leverage is now higher. Base rates: large caps move ±25-35% a year and CRM's realized vol is 47%. I use a 78/22 mixture of a lognormal (median $258, sigma 0.33) and a bear lognormal (median $170, sigma 0.32), which gives P(>= today) of about 0.53, a fat left tail and a median near $240. Research was limited to about 10 queries; the Q2 transcript PDF could not be parsed locally, so a hosted copy of the transcript was used; option data was not consulted.
